# ADR-0013 — The client stack: one React and TypeScript UI, a Tauri 2 shell for macOS, and API types generated by ts-rs

- **Status:** Accepted, 2026-11-09. It was owed at the `r1.s2.w3` close (proposed 2026-11-07, at
  `r1.s2.w3`; `r1.s2.w4` added the Tauri lines). The line was written at `r1.s4.w1`.
- **Date:** 2026-11-07
- **Amended:** 2026-11-09, at `r1.s3.w4`: the chat verbs and the chat stream in the `Transport`
  interface, one bridge route and nine Tauri commands. 2026-11-09, at `r1.s3.w5`: the Agents rail item and
  the chat screens, behind the unchanged `Transport`. 2026-11-10, at `r1.s4.w3`: the Needs you page and the
  Settings rows, behind the `Transport` with ten more methods and one more stream event, and one `verb`
  Tauri command. 2026-11-12, at `r1.s5.w1`: the app tokens, the shared components, the 9a avatar and the
  screenshot line d25. 2026-11-12, at `r1.s5.w2`: the shell, its parts, `NotBuilt`, the dock, the Projects
  page, the pair card, the server menu and the not-connected banner, and the layout of d25 for round 3.
  The round-3 items (`r1.s5.w3`, `w4`, `w5`) fill their own amendment sections at the end of this file.

## Context
- Release 1's first exit criterion: the operator installs the MacBook app, pairs it with draco-desk,
  adds a project and sees it listed. The app needs a UI, and Android follows later (design call D-186).
- ADR-0012 fixed the network API and its login. A webview must not open its own TLS connection (A8):
  the pin check and the device token belong to the native side.
- The approved screens are on the operator's design canvas: dark theme only, the Pulse Trader
  design-system tokens, the shell 2a to 2c, and the pair, server-menu and disconnected screens 3a to 3c.
- Draco-desk cannot run the Tauri app, and `r1.s2` needs an automated line for the UI (d12). The host
  has Chromium 1248 in the Playwright cache.
- The planning audit found that the controller's ledger is local, uncommitted and unbounded (C15), so
  a client must not add request lines of its own by polling.

## Decision

**One UI for every client.** One React and TypeScript bundle, built by Vite, in `apps/ui`. The macOS
app (a Tauri 2 shell, `r1.s2.w4`) and, later, Android load the same bundle.

**One transport interface, two implementations.** The UI reaches the API only through the `Transport`
interface (`docs/contracts/ui-transport.md`): `paired`, `pair`, `status`, `projectList`,
`projectAdd` and `forget`.
- No method takes or returns the device token. It lives on the native side.
- The implementations are the test bridge, `pf-client-bridge` (`crates/pf-client`, the `desktop-bridge`
  fake; a Node script until `r1.s2.w4`), and the Tauri shell's Rust side. Both are `pf-client`'s
  `Transport`, and both make the pinned TLS call with the same verifier (ADR-0012, A8). The bridge
  speaks the bridge protocol over HTTP on `127.0.0.1`. The shell exposes the same six operations as
  Tauri commands.
- The bridge is for d12 and tests. The Mac app never uses it.

**The Tauri shell (`r1.s2.w4`).** `apps/desktop/src-tauri` is a Tauri 2 shell over the same bundle. It
is its own cargo package and workspace (`pulse-factory-desktop`, with a committed `Cargo.lock`), and
the root `Cargo.toml` excludes `apps/desktop`, so no build on draco-desk compiles Tauri.
- **Versions.** `tauri` **2.11.5** and `tauri-build` **2.6.3** (exact `=` pins in its `Cargo.toml`),
  `@tauri-apps/api` **2.11.1** and `@tauri-apps/cli` **2.11.4** (exact pins in `apps/ui/package.json`).
  Tauri's CLI refuses an `@tauri-apps/api` and a `tauri` crate with different minor versions, so the
  four stay on the 2.11 line together. Each is not yanked or deprecated and is more than four months
  old (checked 2026-11-08 against crates.io and the npm registry). Newer releases exist (2.12.x); move
  all four together when the line moves.
- **The app.** Product name `Pulse Factory`, identifier `dev.pulse-factory.desktop`, `bundle.targets`
  `["app"]`, one window of 1440 × 900 with `titleBarStyle` `Transparent` and a hidden title, so the
  shell's own title bar (2a) is the one the operator sees. `build.frontendDist` is `../../ui/dist`.
- **The CSP (A8).** `default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
  connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost`. The bundle's own assets and Tauri's IPC only: the webview
  opens no network connection. No remote domain has IPC access, and the app declares no capability
  file that grants a plugin.
- **Six commands.** `paired`, `pair`, `status`, `project_list`, `project_add` and `forget`, each over
  `Transport<KeychainStore>`. A command returns the wire type or rejects with `{kind, message}`
  (`docs/contracts/ui-transport.md`, "The Tauri commands").
- **The Keychain.** The device token is a generic password in the login Keychain: service
  `pulse-factory.device-token`, account = the server address. The address, the pin and the device record
  are in `pairing.json` in the app's data directory, which holds no secret. `forget()` deletes both.
- **The build.** GitHub's `macos-latest` runner builds `aarch64-apple-darwin` only (the Mac is Apple
  silicon; `universal-apple-darwin` is a one-line change when someone needs it). The workflow signs ad
  hoc (`codesign --force --deep -s -`), verifies (`codesign --verify --deep --strict`), zips with `ditto`
  and uploads the artifact `pulse-factory-macos-app` for 30 days. The signature has no identity, so the
  app is not notarized, and a copy that carries the quarantine flag needs `xattr -dr` (`docs/install.md`).
  Developer ID signing and notarization are the `macos-signing` deferral (expiry `r2`).
- **Licence and openness (ADR-0010).** The app ships from the public repo's CI, with no private input.

**API types are generated (Q6).** `ts-rs` renders them from the Rust types into
`apps/api-client/src/gen/`. A cargo test fails when the committed files drift
(`crates/pf-api/tests/ts_types.rs`). `apps/api-client` is the package `@pulse-factory/api-client`
at version `0.0.0`: types only, no build step. The UI compiles against it, so a drift is a type error.

**No polling (C15).** The UI fetches on start, on opening a page, after an action and on "Retry now".
While connected no timer, interval or focus handler makes a call. After an HTTP refusal it never
retries by itself. The one timer is the retry of `status()` while the server is unreachable (no HTTP
answer, so no request reaches the server and no ledger line is written).

**Dark theme only, with the design-system tokens.** `apps/ui/src/styles/tokens.css` is copied from
the canvas's tokens, with a note that names the source.

**No network fetch at run time.** The Geist and Geist Mono faces come from npm font packages and are
bundled. The built HTML and CSS name no network URL (`scripts/install-ui.sh`'s test, AC-5), and the
bridge serves the bundle with a content security policy for its own origin only.

**The UI line (Q7).** `@playwright/test` **1.64.1** drives Chromium **revision 1248**, which draco-desk
has in `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1248`. d12 (`scripts/demo/ui-pair.sh`) fails with a message when
that browser is missing, and it downloads none.

**Install.** `scripts/install.sh` calls `scripts/install-ui.sh`, which needs Node 22 or later and `npm`,
runs `npm ci` once per tree (when `apps/node_modules` is missing or older than the lock file), builds
the bundle and puts it in `$PF_SHARE_DIR/ui/`.

**Pinned versions.** `apps/` is one npm workspace (`api-client`, `ui`) with one lock file. Every
dependency is pinned exactly: no `^`, no `~`, no range. Checked on 2026-11-07 against the npm registry
(each version exists, is not deprecated and is at least two weeks old, except vitest, which is noted
below; the engines accept Node 22.23.4):

| Package | Version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `react`, `react-dom` | 19.3.1 | the UI |
| `typescript` | 7.0.2 | `tsc --noEmit` is the typecheck |
| `vite` | 8.3.5 | the build (the newest release at least two weeks old) |
| `@vitejs/plugin-react` | 6.1.2 | JSX in Vite 8 |
| `vitest` | 5.1.0 | the unit tests (see the note below) |
| `jsdom` | 30.1.3 | the unit tests' DOM |
| `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/dom`, `@testing-library/user-event` | 16.3.3, 10.4.2, 14.6.8 | the unit tests |
| `@playwright/test` | **1.64.1** | the UI line; the release that drives Chromium 1248 |
| `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`, `@types/node` | 19.3.0, 19.3.0, 22.20.5 | types (`@types/node` follows the Node 22 floor) |
| `@fontsource-variable/geist`, `@fontsource-variable/geist-mono` | 5.3.0 | the faces, bundled |
| `@tauri-apps/api` | 2.11.1 | `invoke` and `isTauri` for the Mac app's transport (`r1.s2.w4`) |
| `@tauri-apps/cli` | 2.11.4 | `tauri build` on the macOS runner (a dev dependency; the install here fetches only the Linux binary) |

`vitest` is 5.1.0 although it is only five days old: with npm 10.9.9 the resolver crashes
(`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`) on every vitest 4.1.x and 5.0.x release that
was tried, and resolves 5.1.0. Check the choice again when npm is upgraded.

The Node floor in the install is "Node 22 or later". The build needs 22.12 or later (Vite 8), and the
unit tests need 22.22.2 or later (jsdom 30). Draco-desk has 22.23.4. `npm ci` warns (`EBADENGINE`) on an
older Node 22.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- **Electron.** It ships its own Chromium and a larger app. Revisit it only if Tauri's macOS webview
  fails the terminal or the editor (the feature list, §0d).
- **A UI that opens its own TLS connection (A8).** A webview cannot read the server key to pin it, and
  it would hold the token where a page script can reach it.
- **A browser client served by the controller (D-156).** Reachability is not authentication, and ADR-0012
  keeps the login on the native side.
- **Polling for "live" data.** It adds a request line to the controller's local, unbounded ledger for
  each tick (C15). The stream comes with `r1.s3`.
- **Hand-written API types.** They drift silently from the Rust types. `ts-rs` and a drift test do not.

## Consequences
- A new client (Android) needs a native side that implements the six methods and the pin check. The
  UI does not change.
- Every wire change reaches the UI as a TypeScript error: change a Rust type, write the generated
  files, and `npm --prefix apps run typecheck --workspace ui` shows what to fix.
- The install now needs Node 22 and `npm` beside the Rust toolchain (`docs/install.md`).
- The bridge protocol is a contract that `pf-client-bridge` keeps
  (`crates/pulse-factory/tests/client_bridge.rs`).
- The Mac app builds only on GitHub's macOS runner. A change to `apps/desktop` or to `pf-client`'s
  macOS code is seen first on a PR's `macos-app` job, not on draco-desk.
- The Mac app's Rust side pulls `pf-api` (the wire types and the code decoder) into its build, and so
  the server's crates. A later spine may split a wire-only crate out (ADR-0012).
- Each later spine that adds a verb to the allowlist (ADR-0012) adds the matching `Transport` method
  and its screen here.

## Verified
- The pair screen (3a): a code without `pf1-` is refused before any call; `code_refused`, `unreachable`,
  `key_changed` (`server key changed: re-pair`) and `rate_limited` each show their text and keep the
  form; the device-name rule holds (`apps/ui/src/test/pair.test.tsx`, 2026-11-07).
- Projects and the sidebar show the server's projects; an add carries a command ID and fetches the
  list once; a retry after `unreachable` reuses the ID; a refusal shows the server's text
  (`apps/ui/src/test/projects.test.tsx`, 2026-11-07).
- The disconnected screen (3c): every kind shows its state; only `unreachable` retries, and only
  `status()`, at 4, 8, 16, 32 and 60 seconds; the other kinds set no timer over ten minutes
  (`apps/ui/src/test/disconnected.test.tsx`, 2026-11-07).
- The UI never polls: connected, thirty minutes of timers and a blurred and focused window make no
  call (`apps/ui/src/test/no-polling.test.tsx`, 2026-11-07).
- The shell: the rail holds exactly Projects and Settings; ⌘B and a click on the selected icon toggle
  the sidebar; the history arrows work; the server menu and Settings show the address, state and last
  call; "Disconnect this Mac" calls `forget()` and names the revoke command; `localStorage` holds only
  the sidebar state (`apps/ui/src/test/shell.test.tsx`, 2026-11-07).
- The bridge pins the key before any byte is sent, answers `key_changed` for a wrong or a changed key
  with zero bytes written, maps every API status to its kind, keeps the token in a mode-0600 file only,
  and prints no token or code. This was checked on the Node bridge (2026-11-07). `pf-client-bridge`
  keeps it: `crates/pf-client/tests/pinned_tls.rs`, `crates/pulse-factory/tests/client_pinned.rs` and
  `client_bridge.rs` (2026-11-08).
- The SPKI of an ECDSA P-256 key is the 91-byte DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, not the 65-byte point that
  Node's `getPeerCertificate().pubkey` returns. `pf-client` reads the SPKI from the DER certificate
  (`crates/pf-client/src/pin.rs`, tested against `rcgen`'s own SPKI, and by the pairing tests, which
  fail on a wrong hash, 2026-11-08).
- The Tauri config names the identifier `dev.pulse-factory.desktop` and the frontend `../../ui/dist`,
  builds `app` only, and has a CSP with `default-src 'self'` and no network origin but Tauri's
  `http://ipc.localhost`. `tauri` is pinned with `=`, and the cargo workspace does not hold the
  desktop package (the AC-7 command of `r1.s2.w4`, 2026-11-08).
- The Mac app's transport invokes the command of each method's name with the arguments of
  `docs/contracts/ui-transport.md`, turns a rejection of each of the nine kinds into a `TransportError`
  of that kind, and `main.tsx` picks it inside Tauri and the bridge elsewhere
  (`apps/ui/src/test/tauri-transport.test.ts`, 2026-11-08).
- `@tauri-apps/api` is pinned exactly with the other npm dependencies
  (`apps/ui/package.json`, AC-11 of `r1.s2.w4`, 2026-11-08).
- The built bundle names no network URL in its HTML or CSS (`scripts/install-ui.sh` with AC-5).
- The whole journey runs in headless Chromium 1248 against the built binary and bundle: pair, add a
  project, revoke the device and see 3c; every request goes to the bridge's origin; no token or code
  is in browser storage, the console or a bridge answer (`scripts/demo/ui-pair.sh`, d12, 2026-11-07).

### Unverified claims
- The Tauri app builds on `macos-latest`, its ad-hoc signature verifies, and `pf-client`'s Keychain
  tests pass there. Draco-desk cannot run any of it. This moves to Verified when the `macos-app` run on
  the item PR is green (the report links the run).
- The Tauri 2 macOS webview runs the same bundle, shows the transparent title bar as the shell's 2a, keeps
  the token in the login Keychain under service `pulse-factory.device-token`, makes the pinned call, and
  opens no connection. Gatekeeper opens the ad-hoc-signed app when it carries no quarantine flag. This
  waits for the d13 walk after the spine merges.
- The six Tauri commands' Rust glue (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`) matches the argument names
  that the UI sends (`deviceName` becomes `device_name`). No test on draco-desk compiles it. The
  `macos-app` build compiles it, and the d13 walk runs it.
- The screens match the canvas pixel for pixel. This item follows the layout, the type, the colours
  and the copy of the approved screens and departs where `SPINE.md` rules it (3a's one code field,
  3b's server row, 3c's retry rule, Q5's rail). The operator compares the screenshots with the canvas.

Revisit this ADR when the Android app is planned, or the macOS webview fails the terminal or the editor.

## Amendment, 2026-11-09 (`r1.s3.w4`)

`r1.s3.w4` adds the chat to the client stack. It keeps the CSP of the Tauri config and the rule that the
app declares no capability file, and it adds no npm dependency.

- **The interface grows.** The Consequences rule "each verb added to the allowlist adds its `Transport` method"
  applies to the seven chat verbs: `sessionList`, `sessionStart`, `sessionSend`, `sessionAnswer`,
  `sessionInterrupt`, `sessionSet` and `sessionEnd`. It also gains `openStream(options, onEvent)`, which
  returns a handle with `close()`. `openStream` never rejects for a stream failure: every failure is one
  `closed` event from either implementation, so a screen handles one path (`docs/contracts/ui-transport.md`).
- **Hand-written transport types.** `SessionStarted`, `SessionEnded`, `StreamEvent`, `StreamOptions` and
  `PairedServer.server` are written by hand in `apps/ui/src/transport/types.ts`, as `PairedServer` is. There
  is no wire type for the answers of `session_start` and `session_end`: the controller's own answers have none,
  and a wire type for them is a later change to `pf-api`. The event envelope is the transport's, and its
  `frame` member is the generated `ChatFrame`.
- **The bridge route.** `GET /bridge/stream` carries the stream to the browser as Server-Sent Events: a
  same-origin `GET` that `default-src 'self'` allows, so the bridge's CSP does not change. A WebSocket would
  need a `connect-src` for `ws://`. Known limit: each open `EventSource` holds one of the browser's six
  HTTP/1.1 connections to the bridge, so the UI follows one session per stream.
- **Nine Tauri commands.** The shell adds `session_list`, `session_start`, `session_send`, `session_answer`,
  `session_interrupt`, `session_set`, `session_end`, `open_stream` and `close_stream`. `open_stream` takes the
  stream options and a `tauri::ipc::Channel<StreamEvent>`, and returns the stream's ID.
- **A Channel, not Tauri's event system.** Tauri's `listen` needs a capability that grants `core:event`, and this
  ADR says the app declares no capability file. A `Channel` is the IPC that Tauri provides for ordered
  streaming to one webview call, and it needs no capability. The webview still opens no network connection.
- **A reload closes the streams.** The shell's `on_page_load` hook calls `Streams::close_all()` when a page
  starts loading, so a reloaded webview leaves no stream open behind a channel that nobody reads.
- **The desktop lock.** `pf-client`'s dependencies grew (`tokio-tungstenite` and `futures-util`), so
  `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock` is refreshed in this item with `cargo metadata`, which compiles nothing.
  Without it the `macos-app` job fails on `--locked`.
- **No timer in the UI.** Neither implementation of the interface sets a timer: the reconnect lives in
  `pf-client` once, for both, so the UI never polls (C15).

### Verified claims (r1.s3.w4)
- Both implementations run one table of cases (`fetch` and `EventSource` mocked, `invoke` and `Channel` mocked):
  each chat method sends its verb or command with its arguments, each of the nine error kinds becomes a
  `TransportError`, `openStream` delivers the same scripted events in order, nothing follows `closed`, a value of
  another shape is dropped, no call holds the word `token`, and no timer is set
  (`apps/ui/src/test/transport-contract.test.ts`, 2026-11-09).
- The names in `generate_handler![…]`, the `#[tauri::command]` functions, `TAURI_COMMANDS` and the contract's
  table are one set, each command's Rust argument names are the `invoke` keys in snake case, and `open_stream`'s
  `on_event` is a `Channel` (`apps/ui/src/test/tauri-commands.test.ts`, 2026-11-09).

### Unverified claims (r1.s3.w4)
- The `Channel` delivers the stream's events, in order, in the Mac app's webview, and the nine commands' Rust glue
  runs. No test on draco-desk compiles `main.rs`. The `macos-app` job compiles it, and the d17 walk runs it.

## Amendment, 2026-11-09 (`r1.s3.w5`)

`r1.s3.w5` builds the Orchestrator chat in the UI. It adds screens behind the `Transport` interface of
`r1.s3.w4` and nothing else to the stack: no npm dependency, no transport method, no Tauri command, no
capability file and no storage key.

- **The Agents rail item and the chat screens.** The rail is Projects and Agents at the top and Settings at
  the bottom (A9). The Agents page is read only: the agents the server lists, the selected agent's defaults,
  and its sessions by project with Open or Start session. A chat is a tab in the title bar. It shows a header
  (project, worktree, branch read live by the server, state, an `unqualified` mark for an override binary,
  the cost and End session), the message stream, approval and question cards that are answered in place, and a
  composer with the runtime's own controls, the context gauge and the cache-warm timer. The sidebar lists each
  project's live sessions.
- **One stream and its reopen rule.** The UI keeps one stream open: the overview while no chat is on screen,
  and the chat on screen otherwise, with `after` the highest `seq` it holds. It opens a new stream only on an
  operator action, when the chat on screen changes, or when the link comes back. `reconnecting` shows a line and
  does nothing; `pf-client` retries (`docs/contracts/ui-transport.md`, "When the UI calls"). A card is pending
  while no held item answers it, so a reload and a reconnect show the same pending cards.
- **No new dependency, storage key or capability.** The reply is plain text, not Markdown. `localStorage` keeps
  `pf.sidebar` only. Every call goes through the `Transport`: no screen calls `fetch`, `EventSource` or
  `WebSocket`, and `scripts/demo/ui-chat.sh` (d19) checks that every request goes to the bridge's origin and
  that no token or code is in storage, the console, the DOM or a bridge answer.
- **The look is not claimed.** The chat screens are built for function from the structure of the approved
  screens 2a to 2c and 6a, and no test judges their look. The pixel claim of the earlier section covers
  `r1.s2`'s screens only. The look of the chat is `r1.s5`'s work, compared against canvas version
  `1794071391-77bb`.
- **Known limits.** The cost in weighted units (wu) is computed at the last turn's cache TTL, because
  `ChatUsage` sums cache writes without the 5-minute and 1-hour split; a split in the wire type is a later
  `pf-api` change. The wire has no persona text for an agent and no session title, so the Agents page shows the
  agent's ids and the chat has no title. A reload forgets which chats were open.

### Verified claims (r1.s3.w5)
- The Agents page, the chat header, each kind of item, the cards (answered in place, `answered`, `withdrawn`
  and `lost`, and still pending after a reconnect and a remount), the composer's controls from the runtime's
  declaration, the gauge, the cache timer, `weightedUnits` and its format, and the stream rule (one stream, the
  reopen only on an operator action or the link's return, nothing after `unauthorized` or `key_changed`) pass
  in `apps/ui/src/test/{agents,chat,composer,cards,chat-stream}.test.tsx`, and no test makes a call for an hour
  (2026-11-09).
- The whole journey runs in headless Chromium through `pf-client-bridge`, against the real controller, the real
  Claude Code adapter and `pf-claude-replay`: Start session on two projects, a `Bash` approval that is still
  pending after a reload and then denied, the cost in wu equal to the CLI's record, an effort change that
  reaches only that chat, and a branch read live. No token or code is in storage, the console, the DOM or a
  bridge answer (`scripts/demo/ui-chat.sh`, d19, 2026-11-09).

### Unverified claims (r1.s3.w5)
- The chat runs in the Mac app's webview: the `Channel` delivers the stream, the approval card is answered and
  the controls work there. The d17 walk on the MacBook checks it, with the real qualified Claude Code copy.
- The look of the chat screens. `r1.s5` compares them with canvas `1794071391-77bb`.

## Amendment, 2026-11-10 (`r1.s4.w3`)

The operator answers the factory in the app: a **Needs you** page and the **Chat policies** rows of the
Settings page. Both are built for function from the structure of the approved screen 3f. The look is
`r1.s5`'s.

- **The `Transport` grows by ten methods and one event, and keeps its kind.** `requests`, `show`,
  `confirmCode`, `answer`, `clear`, `ack`, `settingsGet`, `settingsSet`, `settingsUnset` and `runList`,
  each a thin call of one verb that returns its generated type; the `request_frame` event beside
  `frame`; and `TransportError.refusal`, the word of a refused device verb. No method takes or returns
  the device token or the code's text beyond the one call that spends it.
- **The request frames ride the one stream the app holds (W1).** The controller sends them on every
  stream, the overview included, so Needs you opens no stream of its own: `ChatProvider`'s stream feeds
  the requests state, and the rail's count follows from frames with no call. The page's `requests` read
  when it opens is the correctness path: a fresh page fills its Open requests, its claim and its
  Answered list from that read. No timer, no focus handler, and no second stream: the guards of the
  earlier amendments hold.
- **One `verb` Tauri command, a departure from one command per method (W5).** The interface grows by
  a verb a spine, and a command for each means an edit of `apps/desktop`, a crate that draco-desk never
  builds. `verb {name, args}` calls `pf-client`'s allowlisted `Transport::verb`, so the webview reaches
  no verb a device may not call, and the commands, the handler list, `TAURI_COMMANDS` and the contract's
  table are still one checked set. The ten methods and a later item's go through it. The test bridge
  already had the one generic route.
- **The confirm dialog.** An act is two clicks. The first asks for a one-use confirm code and the dialog
  shows what the code binds (the PR, base, head branch and head SHA, or the exact answer text) and whom
  the act takes the claim from; the second spends it. The claim moves at the final click, so the dialog
  moves nothing, and Cancel, Escape and leaving the page spend nothing. A refusal ends the dialog with
  one line by its word, and a new first click asks for a new code. The code is in memory only: never
  rendered, stored, logged or put in a URL.
- **Known limit (Q2, C1).** The code proves the device, the freshness and the head, not that a person
  pressed the button. A script that holds the device's bridge can do both clicks. The dialog adds no
  user-presence check: that boundary belongs to the Release 2 authority-rules spine.
- **The Settings rows follow the server's registry (W11).** The page names no key. It renders the
  records `settings_get` returns for a chosen project and agent, with the scope each value comes from and

## Amendment, 2026-11-13 (`r1.s5.w3`)

This item is round 3 of `r1.s5`. It gives the Orchestrator chat and the start card the look and the behaviour
of R1 Screens 11a, 11b and 11c. It changes no Rust, no transport, no verb and no `client-api-auth` behaviour.
Three decisions amend this ADR:

- **The chat renders Markdown through an in-house renderer.** `apps/ui/src/components/markdown.tsx` turns a
  reply into React elements from text nodes: paragraphs, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, inline code, fenced code
  blocks, `-` and `1.` lists, and headings as bold lines. It adds **no dependency**, it has **no HTML
  pass-through** (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; HTML in a reply shows as literal text), and it draws **no live
  link**: a link shows as its text with the URL in `title`. The live delta of a turn in progress stays plain
  text until its item is held.
- **The start card has one press.** **Start workflow** asks the server for the one-use confirm code for this
  proposal and this plan (`confirm_code`) and, at once, arms the run with it (`arm`). The code lives in the
  component's state only and never leaves it: it is never shown, stored, logged or put in a URL. After
  `unreachable` on `arm` the code and the command ID stay for the next press; any refusal drops the code and
  the next press asks for a new one. The force of the `client-api-auth` confirm does not change: a fresh code
  for each press, spent once, for this card and this plan, and a second use fails. The card names who started
  the run and when.
- **The window centres and has size limits.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` opens the window at
  1440×860 with `"center": true`, `"minWidth": 1024` and `"minHeight": 640`, so a 14-inch MacBook's visible
  frame holds it. The title bar is an overlay (`"titleBarStyle": "Overlay"`): `main.rs` sets
  `--titlebar-inset` from the page-load event in the desktop app only, and the browser bundle never sets it.
- **The pixel claim.** The claim "the screens match the canvas pixel for pixel" stays unclaimed until the
  operator's ack at the close of `r1.s5`.

## Amendment (`r1.s5.w4`)

This item is round 3 of `r1.s5`. It gives the Needs you page, the Needs-you dock's content, the Agents page and
the Settings page the look and layout of the approved frames 11d, 11g and 11k. It changes no Rust, no verb and
no transport or state file.

- **The one-press confirm.** Each act on Needs you is one press: Send (`answer`), Resume (`clear`) or Approve
  merge (`ack`). Behind the press the app asks for a fresh confirm code and spends it at once (`confirmCode`,
  then the act, with two distinct command IDs). The `client-api-auth` control stays whole: the code is still
  fresh, one-use and bound to this device and this act, and it lives in memory for that press only. The
  two-click confirm panel is gone (grill ruling G1), and so are the claim line and the Runs list: the claim
  shows only in "Answered today", and a run's state shows in the sidebar's Workflow runs group. `ConfirmDialog.tsx`
  stays in the tree, unchanged, with its own component test; Needs you no longer renders it. The refusal lines
  and the retry rules of the dialog carry over to the hook (`needs-you/useConfirmedAct.ts`).
- **A client-only close (Hold).** Hold sets a merge card aside on this Mac (operator ruling R5). It makes no
  call and stores nothing: the held set lives in memory, the request stays open on the server and the rail's
  count still counts it, and the card shows again on a new revision or after a reload. This is a client-only
  close: no server-side hold exists.
- **The `clear` action.** A parked item (a unit request of a kind other than `stop` and `gaps` that lists
  `clear` in `verbs`) gets "Resume <unit>", a one-press `clear` with no `to`. Until this item the app never
  called `clear` (the `r1.s4` retrospective, item 2). The device path (`Act::Clear`) and the API allowlist
  already held it.
- **Accepted gaps**, each a later release or a data limit, not an omission:
  - The chat question's text and option buttons are not in the Needs you card. A device reads a chat's items
    only on the stream that follows that chat (ADR-0012: `session_items` is off the allowlist), so the card
    shows who waits and where, with Open session.
  - The persona text is not shown: the agent record carries none.
  - A parked item's attempt count and asker are not shown: the request carries neither. Its note to the
    Implementer and "Open run view" are `NotBuilt` (R4).
  - The Agents page lists the agents the server lists. Autopilot, Research partner and Plain, agent create and
    edit, Add skill, phone notifications and a permission change are `NotBuilt` or absent.
  - The merge's demo-walk gate is not built (G4: no workflow sets it yet).
  - **The Settings page follows the frame 11k in layout, not in the text of its blocks.** The page names no
    key (W11), so each block's title is the key made readable ("Deny commands", "Propose per min"), not the
    frame's title ("Commands a chat may not run", "Turns a chat may start by itself"). The list block says
    "N entries apply here", where the frame has one sentence per rule. The number blocks have no sentence
    or unit text ("turns, then it waits for you", "per minute"), and `propose_per_min` comes before
    `self_turn_cap`, the reverse of the frame. A title and a sentence per key would put keys in the page.

  parked item in `3f-needs-you` comes through the `overlay` of d25, so the rail's count on the other screens
  does not change.

## Amendment (`r1.s5.w5`)

This item is round 3 of `r1.s5`. It builds the two functions that Projects (11e) and the dialog of 11f left
for it: Add a project and Remove project. It adds two typed methods to the `Transport`, no Tauri command and
no change in `apps/desktop`.

- **Add a project is a dialog** (`components/AddProject.tsx`, `styles/add-project.css`, 700 px wide). The host,
  then how: Browse folder lists the folders of the server's home folder through `transport.folderList`, marks
  the git folders with their branch and the folders that are projects, and names the project after the
  folder. It calls `folder_list` once when it opens and once for each navigation, sets no timer and never
  polls. A plain folder outside a repository gets a tip and an unticked box for `git init`. Clone from URL,
  Create new project and Other hosts are `NotBuilt`.
- **Remove project is a confirm inside the project's block** (`components/RemoveProject.tsx`), not a modal and
  not `ConfirmDialog`: it takes no confirm code. It reads `run_list` once when it opens, lists the live sessions
  from the chat state, and locks its action while a run of the project is active (`RunSummary.project_id`).
  The action calls `transport.projectRemove` with `end_sessions: true`. The page keeps one notice line in the
  place of a block that it removed.
- **The transport seam.** `folderList(args?)` and `projectRemove(args)` join the `Transport` interface. Each is
  one `verb<T>(...)` call in `tauri.ts` and in `bridge.ts`, because both verbs are on the allowlist that
  `pf-client`'s `Transport::verb` checks. `git_init` rides on the generated `ProjectAddArgs`. The
  fake transport records both calls. `apps/api-client/src/index.ts` exports the three new generated types.
- **The stylesheet** `add-project.css` is imported by `AddProject.tsx` (`main.tsx` is not this item's file). The
  bundle therefore places it before `ui.css` and `shell.css`, so each of its overrides carries a second class.
  It joins the token-only check and defines no token.
- **Two screenshots join d25, and three change.** `11e-remove-confirm` (the confirm in `pulse-factory`'s block,
  a workflow running, the action locked) and `11f-add-project` (the dialog, `scratch` picked, the `git init`
  tip) are new. `2c-projects`, `3b-server-menu` and `3c-disconnected` change because the Projects page behind
  them gains the header button and the remove buttons. The other screenshots are byte for byte as before.
  d12 now adds a folder with `git init`, removes the project and adds it again, against a controller whose
  home folder is a temp directory.

## Amendment (`r1.s6.w1`)

This item is round 1 of `r1.s6`. It closes the second gap walk's gaps in the title bar, the server's name, the
not-connected state, the server icon and the Pair button. It changes no Rust, no verb, no transport file and no
dependency (AC-10).

- **One source of the server's name.** `ConnectionProvider` makes **one** `status()` call when it mounts (no
  timer; the no-polling rule holds), through `call()`, so a down kind marks the link down as any call does. It
  is no `retry()`, so it refetches no page. The connection keeps the `server` of every `status()` answer: this
  call, the retry and Settings' call. `apps/ui/src/state/connection.tsx` exports the pure `serverNameOf(paired,
  learned?)` and the hook `useServerName()`: the learned name, else the pairing's `server.name`, else the stored
  name, else the address. All nine former `server.server?.name ?? server.address` sites use one of them
  (`useServerName()` inside the provider, `serverNameOf(paired)` on the pair screen, which renders outside it).
  The pair-success heading reads "Connected to <name>". "No server" before pairing stays (frame 11j).
- **P1: the stored name, and its limit.** The last name an answer gave is kept in `localStorage` under
  `pf.server-name` as `{address, name}`, read and written in a `try`, and used before the first answer when the
  address matches the pairing's. It is a label only: never used for trust, routing or a call. `pf-client` keeps
  the server's name **in memory only** (`note_server`), not with the pairing, so a first launch after pairing
  with the server down, before any answer, shows the address. Storing the name with the pairing is a
  `crates/pf-client` change and is out of scope here.
- **P2: the derived state "not connected".** One display state: the link is down, **or** the chat stream is
  `reconnecting`. It adds no state to the connection's machine and no timer. The banner (11i's copy for both
  causes), the dimmed page, the "As of <time>, when <name> was last reachable" subtitle and the grey pill with
  the time and no dock toggle key on it (`useNotConnected()` in `state/chat.tsx`). `ChatStatus` carries the
  stream's `retry_in_ms`, so the banner counts down on a display tick that makes no call. `StreamLine` no
  longer shows `reconnecting`; it keeps showing a stream that `closed` with a refusal or a server error, with
  its Reconnect button (G8).
- **The title bar is the same on every page** (W2-2, NG-2). Needs you and Settings keep the Projects tab, the
  chat tabs, New tab and the need-you pill with its dock toggle, and hide only the sidebar toggle. The active
  page tab (Projects with a chat tab open, Agents, Needs you, Settings) carries a × (NG-3). **P3:** the ×
  closes the page and shows the last chat tab the operator used, else Projects.
- **The server icon** (NG-22): Lucide's `server` joins `icon-nodes.ts` and is used on the server menu's tile
  and Settings' server tile. **Pair** (NG-24, KL-6): the button is disabled, grey, while the code field is
  empty or blank and while pairing runs; `IconSize` gains 22 for the pair tile.
- **The seams for round 2.** `icon-nodes.ts` holds three marked, empty sections for `r1.s6.w2`, `r1.s6.w3` and
  `r1.s6.w4`, and this file holds three empty amendment sections, one for each, below.
- **The screenshots.** d25 keeps the pairing as the Mac gives it (no name in `PAIRED`), so the name in each
  screenshot came from `status`. The `unreachable` mode answers the first `status` and fails every call after
  it. Six of the fifteen screenshots change (`3a-pair`, `3b-server-menu`, `3c-disconnected`, `3f-needs-you`,
  `6a-agents`, `settings`); the other nine are byte for byte as before.
